title: Other Scales
intro: Beyond major, minor and the modes, a handful of other scales turn up again and again: the pentatonic scales of folk and rock, the blues scale, and the symmetric scales of Debussy, Messiaen and jazz.

blocks.text: The major pentatonic leaves out 4̂ and 7̂ of the major scale: C D E G A. With no semitones it has no strong dissonances, so any of its notes sound good together, which is why it is the scale of so much folk music worldwide, and why the black keys of the piano (G♭ A♭ B♭ D♭ E♭) are a pentatonic scale. The minor pentatonic is its relative: A C D E G.

The blues scale adds a flattened fifth (the 'blue note') to the minor pentatonic: A C D E♭ E G. In the blues, singers and guitarists bend the third and seventh between minor and major, so 'blue notes' are really zones of pitch rather than exact keys; the piano imitates them with crushed grace notes such as E♭ into E.

items: Whole-tone: six notes a whole step apart, C D E F♯ G♯ A♯. Only two exist (on C and on C♯). Every triad in it is augmented, so it has no tonic pull; Debussy used it for blurred, floating harmony ('Voiles').

Octatonic (diminished): alternating half and whole steps, eight notes, C D♭ E♭ E F♯ G A B♭. Only three exist. Rimsky-Korsakov, Stravinsky and Messiaen used it; jazz players use the half–whole form over dominant ♭9 chords.
Augmented (hexatonic): alternating minor thirds and semitones, C E♭ E G A♭ B.

Harmonic and melodic minor modes: Phrygian dominant (5th mode of harmonic minor, E F G♯ A B C D in A minor) is the sound of flamenco and klezmer; the altered scale (7th mode of melodic minor) is used over altered dominants in jazz.
Hungarian minor (A B C D♯ E F G♯) and the double harmonic (A B♭ C♯ D E F G♯) have two augmented seconds.

Non-Western systems divide the octave differently: Indian raga uses 22 shrutis as a pool of fine pitch distinctions; Arabic maqam uses intervals of about three quarters of a tone; Javanese slendro divides the octave into five roughly equal steps. They are not 'out of tune' Western scales but separate systems.

blocks.title: Pentatonic
blocks.text: Spell the D major pentatonic and its relative minor pentatonic.
solution: D major is D E F♯ G A B C♯; drop 4̂ (G) and 7̂ (C♯): D E F♯ A B. Its relative minor pentatonic starts on 6̂ = B: B D E F♯ A.
blocks.answer: D E F♯ A B; B D E F♯ A

blocks.title: Symmetry
blocks.text: Why are there only two whole-tone scales and only three octatonic scales?
solution: The whole-tone scale repeats when transposed by a whole step, so transposing by 0 or 1 semitone gives all of them: two. The octatonic repeats under transposition by a minor third (3 semitones), so 0, 1 and 2 semitones give three different ones. Messiaen called these 'modes of limited transposition'.
blocks.answer: They map onto themselves under transposition by 2 and 3 semitones
